newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PICK MAY BEGIN PRODUCING MINERAL WATER.
newsitem.headline: PICK MAY BEGIN PRODUCING MINERAL WATER.

text.p: Hungarian meat processor Pick said on Friday it may go into producing mineral water after discovering a source on its company premises in Szeged, southern Hungary.
"We have the licences to exploit the water and tests show that it contains minerals which qualify it as mineral water," Pick's finance director Lukacs Vamosi told Reuters.
"Test production has started but it won't be a very big investment. If it proves to be profitable we will spend more on it later."
Vamosi said the water had been discovered during an effort to dig wells as a cost-saving exercise.
"We use large amounts of mains water in producing our salami and as there is lots of underground water around Szeged we tried digging wells on our own land to save production costs," he said.
The management will ask shareholders' approval for its plan to exploit the source at the company's annual general meeting on April 28.

The board of directors said on Wednesday they would propose a 20 percent dividend payout, or 200 forints per share, on the 1996 results, and would seek authorisation to organise a 10 percent equity raise.
The company paid a 15 percent dividend last year.
Pick posted a consolidated pre-tax profit of 2.48 billion forints on net sales of 28.56 billion in 1996.
At 1059 GMT Pick shares stood at 11,500 forints down 200 on Thursday's close.
